:::{#exr-basis-practice}
#### Testing whether $(1, 1)$ and $(1, -1)$ form a basis of $\reals^2$

Describing every vector in $\reals^2$ through $(1, 1)$ and $(1, -1)$ instead of the axes
works only if those two vectors form a [basis](#def-basis).
Let

$$
\vecf{a}_1 = \sbmat{1 \\ 1},
\qquad
\vecf{a}_2 = \sbmat{1 \\ -1}.
$$

Is $\vecf{a}_1, \vecf{a}_2$ a basis of $\reals^2$?

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

Check both conditions of @def-basis.
For spanning,
look for $c_1$ and $c_2$ with $c_1 \vecf{a}_1 + c_2 \vecf{a}_2 = \tp{(x, y)}$.

:::

:::
